findings.title: #1141 AC2 is not met: the whole browser suite was not run twice, only the one touched spec
findings.evidence: Ticket line: '- [ ] The whole browser suite green twice with no B4 red.' Report: 'The LITERAL whole browser suite is 54 spec files ... running it twice was outside this session's practical time budget'; what ran was work-question-walk.spec.ts alone, 14 cells, twice (1.7m and 1.4m). For this ticket the substitution is not equivalent: the ticket's own summary records B4 'red exactly once in each of three whole-suite runs ... green in every second run and in every isolated re-run (14 of 14, twice each time)', so an isolated green run is precisely the condition under which the defect has never shown, and two of them are not evidence against the load-sensitive race.
findings.required_fix: Run the full 54-spec browser suite twice on the integrator's rig (or in the gate) and record B4's result in both, before #1141 is closed; otherwise record the residual against the ticket instead of closing it as done.

findings.title: #1044 AC3 is met for one leg of the db-live-gates intake chain only, and that leg went red twice on this branch
findings.evidence: Ticket line: '- [ ] The driver of .github/actions/db-live-gates green five consecutive times on a fresh database; CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true pnpm lint exit 0; the runtime test file once under WSL as user runner.' Lint (exit 0) and the WSL run (20 pass / 0 fail) are met. The driver is not: the report runs only leg 3 (intake-batch-e2e.mjs) and states legs 1 and 2 (intake-e2e.mjs, intake-admission-e2e.mjs) 'cannot be run on this rig at all', because waitForQueueDrain censuses roughly 76 permanently unbindable tasks inherited from the clara_l08 template. Of the 9 branch rounds of leg 3, rounds 5 and 9 exited 1 at intake-batch-e2e.mjs:650 ('exactly one op receipt per live child (16 of 17)' and '(29 of 31)'). The 'FIVE CONSECUTIVE GREEN' that fills the FINAL5 row comes from an orchestrator addendum quoting the tail of background task b1v86pxjf, not from the implementer's own per-round table, and it is still leg 3 alone.
findings.required_fix: The integrator must run the whole db-live-gates driver (all three intake legs) on a genuinely fresh database or disposable cluster before #1044 is closed, and must act on the report's follow-up 3 (file intake-batch-e2e.mjs:650 as its own defect): db-live-gates is a required check, so a load-sensitive red there blocks the wave whatever its cause.

findings.title: #1131's entire deliverable has never been executed inside the drill it lives in, and that drill is a required per-PR gate
findings.evidence: Ticket AC1: 'The contract-refusal exit code is covered by some automated test that can run without a hand-maintained WDK World clone.' The coverage added is a 70-line block in packages/runtime/tests/two-build-cutover-e2e.mjs (noContracts / requiredContracts / cliC, after cliA). The lane report's own gate table reads 'New/touched test file, full execution | *not run this session*', and its Anything-unverified section states the block is proven only by a hand-run CLI against a clone and 'does not prove the new block is free of a scope/variable-naming mistake that only a real run inside main()'s actual execution context ... would catch'. That file runs inside db-live-gates (action.yml:488), which feeds the required 'ci' context on every code PR, so a wrong assertion reds the required gate for the whole repo. I re-read the block's inputs and they do resolve (preflight({query,supported,contracts,scope}) matches lib/rollback-preflight.mjs:779; violations carry requirement/contract per :203-204; preRuleBodies, requiredBodies, runPreflightCli, w1, w2, query are all in scope at lines 966-990), so this is a residual risk rather than a demonstrated defect - but the acceptance criterion is 'covered by an automated test', and no automated run of it exists.
findings.required_fix: Run packages/runtime/tests/two-build-cutover-e2e.mjs end to end once (integrator rig, or the first db-live-gates run) and record its '[tb-e2e] preflight CLI: --supported <body-complete roster>, no --supported-contracts, exits 1 ...' line before closing #1131.

findings.title: #1127's notification channel is unproven, and if the grant is refused its own failure is invisible - the exact condition the ruling exists to end
findings.evidence: Ruling (issue #1127, comment of 2026-09-24): 'Yes: wire the weekly scheduled CI dispatch's failure to a visible notification.' The implementation is ci.yml's notify-schedule-failure job running 'gh issue comment 1127' under a job-level 'permissions: issues: write'. ci.yml carried no permissions block anywhere before this change, and it is the repo's ONLY workflow (ls .github/workflows/ -> ci.yml), so nothing here has ever exercised a write-scoped GITHUB_TOKEN. The lane report says so itself: 'Whether gh issue comment succeeds against the live default GITHUB_TOKEN with only the job's own issues: write grant (rather than ... being blocked by an org-level token-permission default narrower than what a job-level permissions block can widen) is unverified.' If the grant is refused the job fails on a scheduled run - and nobody reads scheduled runs, which is the ticket's own premise.
findings.required_fix: Before closing #1127: confirm the repository/organisation 'Workflow permissions' setting lets a job request write scopes, and watch a real scheduled (or deliberately failed dispatch) run actually post the comment. Until a comment lands on an issue, #1127 is wired but not proven.

findings.title: #1127 routes its notification to issue #1127 itself, which this wave closes
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/ci.yml:658 hardcodes 'gh issue comment 1127', and packages/db/tests/ci-schedule-notify.test.mjs's p1127.notify.channel pins that literal. #1127 is the ticket this lane delivers, so it is closed when the wave lands, and the standing channel for every future weekly red becomes a closed issue nobody has reason to reopen. The ruling does allow 'a GitHub issue comment', so this is inside its letter, and the lane report flags it as its own first follow-up.
findings.required_fix: Owner/orchestrator call: either keep #1127 open as the standing CI-health thread and say so in the issue, or mint a dedicated ci-health tracking issue and point both the workflow line and p1127.notify.channel at it in one follow-up.

findings.title: #1141 deleted B4's named not.toBe("BODY") assertion, the one carrying the cell's own title
findings.evidence: The diff removes both expect(focused.tag, 'focus was dumped onto the document body when the row disappeared').not.toBe('BODY') and the tag field from the evaluate payload, replacing them with expect.poll(...).toBe('H2'). toBe('H2') subsumes not-BODY, so no coverage is lost in substance; what is lost is the named failure message for the defect the cell's own title states ('the row leaves without dumping focus'), and the ticket asked for the cell to be corrected, not narrowed. summary: Eight tickets, ten findings, and none of them is a requirement implemented wrongly. #1128, #1129 and #1126 are clean on the spec axis and re-ran green here. The weight is all on evidence: #1141 misses BOTH of its evidence acceptance criteria (no reproduced red, no whole-suite run), #1044 proves one leg of the three-leg db-live-gates driver and that leg went red twice on this branch, #1131's whole deliverable has never executed inside the drill it lives in, and #1127's notification channel has never posted a comment. Each gap is disclosed in the lane's own reports; none of them is closable from this worktree.
